10. Worked Example
The example below directly demonstrates formatting raw text into instruction-response pairs, already covered in this topic, ready for training.

code.content:
raw_examples = [
    {"task": "summarize", "input": "The cat sat on the mat and slept all day.", "output": "A cat slept on a mat."},
    {"task": "translate", "input": "good morning", "output": "bonjour"},
]

def format_instruction_pair(example):
    # already covered as instruction response pairs in this topic
    instruction = f"{example['task'].capitalize()}: {example['input']}"
    response = example["output"]
    return f"{instruction}\nResponse: {response}"

print("Formatted instruction-response pairs (already covered in this topic):\n")
for example in raw_examples:
    formatted = format_instruction_pair(example)
    print(formatted)
    print("---")

# already covered as still next token prediction underneath in this topic
print("\nDuring training, the model still just predicts the next token at every position,")
print("already covered in Next Token Prediction, but now learning from this instruction-shaped data")

blocks.content: Running this example shows raw task data reformatted into a consistent instruction-response structure, exactly the formatting already covered in this topic, ready to be trained on using the same underlying next-token prediction mechanism.

blocks.text: 11. Key Takeaways

items: Instruction tuning shifts focus from parameter efficiency to the shape of the training data itself.
A pretrained model only continues text plausibly; it has no built-in notion of following instructions.
Instruction tuning trains on explicit instruction-response pairs instead of plain continuation text.
The underlying training mechanism is still next token prediction; only the data structure changes.
Real datasets cover many different task types at once, mixed together during training.
This diverse coverage lets the model generalize to entirely new, unseen instructions.
LoRA and prompt tuning focus on how training happens; instruction tuning focuses on the data itself.
It can combine with LoRA or full fine-tuning as the actual training mechanism underneath.
Next up: Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT), the broader training approach instruction tuning is a form of.
